newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SembCorp may offer shares in Jurong deal.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp may offer shares in Jurong deal.

text.p: SembCorp Ltd said on Monday it was considering offering new SembCorp shares and cash as an alternative to just cash in its takeover offer for Jurong Shipyard.
In a statement issued by SembCorp's financial adviser, Standard Chartered Merchant Bank Asia Ltd, SembCorp said it will be seeking approval from shareholders for the share cum cash alternative.
It said: "Shareholders should note the share alternative is only under consideration and the directors may or may not proceed with it."
SembCorp had earlier signed an agreement with Jurong to merge the shipyard operations of the two companies.
Under the deal, SembCorp will inject its shipyard assets into Jurong, which will in turn pay for them by issuing new Jurong shares at Singapore $6.80 each.
The merger will result in SembCorp increasing its stake in Jurong to 38.6 percent from about 23 percent currently.
Under Singapore takeover laws, SembCorp will have to make a general offer for all outstanding Jurong shares at S$6.80 a share in cash.
Standard Chartered said SembCorp directors want to have the discretion not to proceed with the share alternative if they think such an issue would not be in the interest of SembCorp.
It added that the SembCorp directors will also have the discretion to determine the share price of each new SembCorp share to be issued as part of the takeover.

The price will take into account the last transacted price of SembCorp shares traded on the date of the announcement of the share alternative and the attractiveness of the terms of the share alternative to Jurong shareholders, said the statement.
